text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish newspapers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Parliament planning expansion at nearby lot, currently a park enclosing a restaurant.
- Thousands of unemployed betweeN 15 and 19 years old may be invisIble in labour ministry statistics since they have no right to benefits and little incentive to register as job seekers.
- Ice in bays of the Gulf of Finland is exceptionally thin and dangerous this winter.
- Government allocates nine million markka to fight violence against women as part of a programme of equality between the sexes.
- Parliament Speaker Riitta Uosukainen beats President Martti Ahtisaari with 25 percent to his 18 percent in poll of who would be elected next President.
- Parliament seeks agreement on controversial liberalisation of business opening hours from the basis of allowing shops on more Sundays than now -- but not every Sunday.
- Merita holding and investment company Sponsor interested in buying parts of wholesale and retail group Tuko from Kesko.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Hyatt Hotels demand 500 million markka compensation from state-controlled SKOPBank from Virgin Islands hotel project, Hyatt lawyer says.
- Nokia Communicator will get access to more services as a result of Californian system provider Geoworks' deal with two new service providers, Internet Travel Network and M.A.I.D.
- The museum of modern art Kiasma, currently under construction, has signed sponsorhip agreements worth almost 20 million with Aamulehti, MTV3, Nokia, Sokos, the post and Telecom Finland.
- The financial supervision authority Rata has granted the world's largest investment fund Fidelity permission to start marketing itself in Finland. Fidelity's funds are worth some $520 million.
DEMARI
- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen surprised audience by reciting poems in three languages on anniversary of national poet Runeberg.
AAMULEHTI
- Governing parties' MPs near a compromise on shop opening hours liberalisation.
- Nokian Paperi Oy plans to build small 60 million markka tissue paper mill in Russia.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Kesko's talks with Wihuri-yhtyma on the sale of Tuko have ended with no result, Wihuri chairman says.
- Turku's statue of Olympic hero Paavo Nurmi to be moved seven metres.
